claim: The zebrafish is an appealing vertebrate model system with a simple, yet functionally conserved heart.
source: The zebrafish is an appealing vertebrate model system with a simple, yet functionally conserved heart.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about zebrafish as a model organism.

claim: Light sheet microscopy has proven to be supremely suited for obtaining in vivo recordings of the intact embryonic zebrafish heart.
source: Light sheet microscopy has proven to be supremely suited for obtaining in vivo recordings of the intact embryonic zebrafish heart (Chi et al., 2008; Scherz et al., 2008; Arnaout et al., 2007; Trivedi et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior work demonstrating this capability.

claim: Whole cardiac cycles have been reconstructed in 4D (3D + time) using post-acquisition synchronization of high-speed light sheet movies in a z-stack.
source: Whole cardiac cycles have been reconstructed in 4D (3D + time) using post-acquisition synchronization of high-speed light sheet movies in a z-stack.
evidence: This describes a methodological approach that has been previously established.

claim: The effective temporal resolution of post-acquisition synchronized light sheet microscopy is about 400 volumes per second.
source: The resulting effective temporal resolution of about 400 volumes per second (Mickoleit et al., 2014) is unmatched by other in vivo volumetric imaging techniques such as light sheet microscopy with electrically focus-tunable lenses or swept, confocally-aligned planar excitation (Bouchard et al., 2015; Fahrbach et al., 2013; Hou et al., 2014; Liebling et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mickoleit et al., 2014 and comparison with other cited techniques.

claim: The temporal resolution of about 400 volumes per second is unmatched by other in vivo volumetric imaging techniques.
source: The resulting effective temporal resolution of about 400 volumes per second (Mickoleit et al., 2014) is unmatched by other in vivo volumetric imaging techniques such as light sheet microscopy with electrically focus-tunable lenses or swept, confocally-aligned planar excitation (Bouchard et al., 2015; Fahrbach et al., 2013; Hou et al., 2014; Liebling et al., 2005).
evidence: Comparative claim supported by citations to alternative techniques.

claim: A light sheet microscope was built tailored for high-speed imaging of the heart in the living zebrafish embryo.
source: We built a light sheet microscope tailored for high-speed imaging of the heart in the living zebrafish embryo.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental setup performed by the authors.

claim: The magnification and camera readout were fine-tuned to balance field of view and spatial and temporal sampling to record cardiac activation in the entire heart with cellular precision.
source: By fine-tuning the magnification and restricting camera readout to the center area of the chip, we balanced the field of view and the spatial and temporal sampling to record cardiac activation in the entire heart with cellular precision (Materials and methods).
evidence: Description of methodological optimization performed by the authors.

claim: Post-acquisition synchronization can be extended to visualizing calcium transients in cardiac myocytes across the entire heart of living embryonic zebrafish expressing GCaMP5G.
source: We investigated whether post-acquisition synchronization could be extended to visualizing calcium transients in cardiac myocytes across the entire heart of living embryonic zebrafish expressing the fluorescent calcium reporter GCaMP5G under the myl7 promoter (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Research question investigated by the authors with reference to experimental data in figures.

claim: The genetically expressed calcium reporter GCaMP5G provides a specific, consistent and non-invasive readout of cardiomyocyte activity in vivo.
source: The genetically expressed calcium reporter provides a specific, consistent and non-invasive readout of cardiomyocyte activity in vivo (Figure 1b, Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: Characterization of the reporter supported by experimental data shown in figures and videos.

claim: The calcium signal from GCaMP5G had good and stable fluorescent yield at low excitation power, superior to genetically expressed voltage reporters.
source: In a side-by-side comparison, the calcium signal had good and stable fluorescent yield at low excitation power, superior to genetically expressed voltage reporters.
evidence: Comparative experimental result from side-by-side comparison performed by the authors.

claim: The calcium signal faithfully reports presence and timing of cell activation.
source: Importantly, the calcium signal faithfully reports presence and timing of cell activation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) (Kralj et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and citation to Kralj et al., 2011.

claim: Electrical excitation and mechanical contraction were decoupled by inhibiting the formation of the calcium-sensitive regulatory complex within sarcomeres using a morpholino against tnnt2a.
source: To prevent interference of tissue movement and deformation with observed signals, we decoupled electrical excitation and mechanical contraction by inhibiting the formation of the calcium-sensitive regulatory complex within sarcomeres, using a morpholino against tnnt2a (Materials and methods).
evidence: Description of experimental intervention performed by the authors.

claim: Zebrafish embryos were mounted in low concentration agarose inside polymer tubes for precise optical investigation without anesthesia.
source: By mounting zebrafish embryos in low concentration agarose inside polymer tubes, we could position the embryos for precise optical investigation without anesthesia (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: Description of sample preparation method with reference to figure.

claim: A fluorescent nuclear marker (myl7:H2A-mCherry) was recorded to attribute calcium dynamics to individual cardiomyocytes.
source: To attribute calcium dynamics to individual cardiomyocytes, we also recorded a fluorescent nuclear marker (myl7:H2A-mCherry).
evidence: Description of experimental approach for cell identification.

claim: The high temporal (400 Hz) and spatial sampling (0.5 µm pixel size) was adequate for computing normalized average calcium transients throughout the cardiac cycle for each cell across the entire heart.
source: The high temporal (400 Hz) and spatial sampling (0.5 µm pixel size) was adequate for computing normalized average calcium transients throughout the cardiac cycle for each cell across the entire heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Video 3, Materials and methods).
evidence: Assessment of imaging parameters supported by data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Rise times were shortest for atrial muscle cells, intermediate in the atrio-ventricular canal (AVC), and longest for ventricular cardiomyoctes by 52 hpf.
source: Rise times were shortest for atrial muscle cells, intermediate in the atrio-ventricular canal (AVC), and longest for ventricular cardiomyoctes (Figure 1c''), in keeping with higher vertebrates where atrial myocyte contraction is faster than that of ventricular cells (Brandenburg et al., 2016).
evidence: Experimental observation supported by data in Figure 1c'' and comparison with cited literature.

claim: In higher vertebrates, atrial myocyte contraction is faster than that of ventricular cells.
source: Rise times were shortest for atrial muscle cells, intermediate in the atrio-ventricular canal (AVC), and longest for ventricular cardiomyoctes (Figure 1c''), in keeping with higher vertebrates where atrial myocyte contraction is faster than that of ventricular cells (Brandenburg et al., 2016).
evidence: Established fact from the literature cited.

claim: A positive correlation exists between rise time and position of cells along the midline, with a clear discontinuity at the AVC.
source: We identified a positive correlation between rise time and position of cells along the midline, with a clear discontinuity at the AVC (Figure 1—figure supplement 4b), illustrating emergence of chamber-specific patterns of individual cell activation properties across the heart.
evidence: Quantitative analysis result supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4b.

claim: Cardiac activation in the early linear heart tube is slow and near-uniform.
source: While cardiac activation in the early linear heart tube is slow and near-uniform, the chambered heart shows areas of elevated conduction velocity (Dehaan, 1961; de Jong et al., 1992; Moorman et al., 1998; Chi et al., 2008; Panáková et al., 2010).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The chambered heart shows areas of elevated conduction velocity.
source: While cardiac activation in the early linear heart tube is slow and near-uniform, the chambered heart shows areas of elevated conduction velocity (Dehaan, 1961; de Jong et al., 1992; Moorman et al., 1998; Chi et al., 2008; Panáková et al., 2010).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Biophysical and biological conduction velocities show differences between and within anatomical regions of the heart.
source: Our analysis revealed that biophysical and biological conduction velocities show differences between and within anatomical regions of the heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: Result from the authors' analysis supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: Particularly slow conduction occurs between the most proximal atrial cells and between the cells of the AVC.
source: Either descriptor identifies particularly slow conduction between the most proximal atrial cells and between the cells of the AVC, while faster conduction is seen among working myocardial cells of the atrium and ventricle.
evidence: Observation from the authors' analysis of conduction patterns.

claim: Faster conduction is seen among working myocardial cells of the atrium and ventricle.
source: Either descriptor identifies particularly slow conduction between the most proximal atrial cells and between the cells of the AVC, while faster conduction is seen among working myocardial cells of the atrium and ventricle.
evidence: Observation from the authors' analysis of conduction patterns.

claim: In the atrium, there is a bias towards higher biophysical speeds due to larger cell dimensions.
source: In the atrium, there is a bias towards higher biophysical speeds, due to larger cell dimensions (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 4c).
evidence: Inference from data analysis supported by figures showing cell dimensions and conduction speeds.

claim: At 52 hpf, less than 10 cells per heart serve as activation origins.
source: We found that, at 52 hpf, less than 10 cells per heart serve as activation origins.
evidence: Quantitative finding from the authors' analysis of pacemaker cells.

claim: Pacemaker cells are located in the sinus venosus at the heart's inflow side at 52 hpf.
source: They are located in the sinus venosus at the heart's inflow side, which is a homologue of the primary cardiac pacemaker region in adult heart (Poon and Brand, 2013).
evidence: Spatial localization finding supported by citation to comparative anatomy.

claim: The sinus venosus is a homologue of the primary cardiac pacemaker region in adult heart.
source: They are located in the sinus venosus at the heart's inflow side, which is a homologue of the primary cardiac pacemaker region in adult heart (Poon and Brand, 2013).
evidence: Established anatomical homology supported by citation.

claim: The ring-like arrangement of pacemaker cells, together with a preferential orientation of myocardial cells perpendicular to the inflow-outflow direction, generates the initial planar 'ring-like' activation front that propagates evenly into the atrium.
source: Our data further show that the ring-like arrangement of pacemaker cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 7), together with a preferential orientation of myocardial cells in that region perpendicular to the inflow-outflow direction (Auman et al., 2007) (Figure 1—figure supplement 8), generates the initial planar 'ring-like' activation front that propagates evenly into the atrium.
evidence: Mechanistic inference from the authors' data combined with cited structural information.

claim: Myocardial cells in the pacemaker region have a preferential orientation perpendicular to the inflow-outflow direction.
source: Our data further show that the ring-like arrangement of pacemaker cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 7), together with a preferential orientation of myocardial cells in that region perpendicular to the inflow-outflow direction (Auman et al., 2007) (Figure 1—figure supplement 8), generates the initial planar 'ring-like' activation front that propagates evenly into the atrium.
evidence: Structural observation supported by citation and figure.

claim: Torsion associated with cardiac looping is most pronounced around the AVC.
source: Interestingly, by following the orientation of this reference system along the midline, we noticed torsion associated with the cardiac looping, which is most pronounced around the AVC (Männer, 2000; Christoffels et al., 2000; Harvey, 2002).
evidence: Observation from the authors' geometric analysis supported by citations to prior work on cardiac looping.

claim: A clear asymmetry in conduction speeds exists between cells at the inner and the outer curvatures.
source: A clear asymmetry in conduction speeds between cells at the inner and the outer curvatures was apparent in this representation (Figure 1f).
evidence: Observation from the authors' analysis shown in Figure 1f.

claim: The activation wave travelled smoothly in a ring-like fashion along the heart, irrespective of differences in conduction speeds.
source: Irrespective of these differences, however, the activation wave travelled smoothly in a ring-like fashion along the heart, as indicated by the isochronal lines in the cylindrical projection (Figure 1—figure supplement 9).
evidence: Observation from the authors' analysis supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 9.

claim: During the period between 36 and 52 hpf, ventricular cell number increased by about 45%.
source: During the crucial period between 36 and 52 hpf, ventricular cell number increased by about 45%, the initial heart tube developed into a two-chambered organ, the midline of the heart became increasingly curved and twisted (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and the activation frequency increased – all signs of organ maturation.
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the authors' longitudinal study.

claim: The initial heart tube developed into a two-chambered organ between 36 and 52 hpf.
source: During the crucial period between 36 and 52 hpf, ventricular cell number increased by about 45%, the initial heart tube developed into a two-chambered organ, the midline of the heart became increasingly curved and twisted (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and the activation frequency increased – all signs of organ maturation.
evidence: Morphological observation from the authors' longitudinal study.

claim: The midline of the heart became increasingly curved and twisted between 36 and 52 hpf.
source: During the crucial period between 36 and 52 hpf, ventricular cell number increased by about 45%, the initial heart tube developed into a two-chambered organ, the midline of the heart became increasingly curved and twisted (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and the activation frequency increased – all signs of organ maturation.
evidence: Geometric observation from the authors' longitudinal study shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The activation frequency increased between 36 and 52 hpf.
source: During the crucial period between 36 and 52 hpf, ventricular cell number increased by about 45%, the initial heart tube developed into a two-chambered organ, the midline of the heart became increasingly curved and twisted (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and the activation frequency increased – all signs of organ maturation.
evidence: Functional measurement from the authors' longitudinal study.

claim: Despite a net increase in cell numbers, the time required for activation to propagate from inflow to outflow decreased during development.
source: In spite of a net increase in cell numbers, the time required for activation to propagate from inflow to outflow decreased.
evidence: Observation from the authors' analysis of developmental changes.

claim: A progressive crowding of calcium transient activation dynamics indicated maturation of cells, with two groups differentiating from the early more homogeneous pattern: working cardiomyocytes in atrium and ventricle.
source: A progressive crowding of calcium transient activation dynamics indicated maturation of cells, with two groups differentiating from the early more homogeneous pattern: working cardiomyocytes in atrium and ventricle (Figure 2a–f).
evidence: Interpretation of developmental changes observed in the data shown in Figure 2a–f.

claim: At 36 hpf, activation propagated evenly across the myocardium, compatible with peristalsis.
source: At 36 hpf, activation propagated evenly across the myocardium, compatible with peristalsis.
evidence: Observation from the authors' analysis at early developmental stage.

claim: Calcium dynamics became increasingly structured during development from 36 to 52 hpf.
source: Subsequently, calcium dynamics became increasingly structured.
evidence: Observation of developmental progression from the authors' longitudinal study.

claim: By 52 hpf, propagation of activation was fast across atrium and ventricle, while it remained slow in the AVC.
source: By 52 hpf, propagation of activation was fast across atrium and ventricle, while it remained slow in the AVC (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: Observation from the authors' analysis at 52 hpf shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a.

claim: With organ maturation during 16 hr (36-52 hpf), cells in the ventricular part of the network showed longer calcium transient rise time.
source: With organ maturation during these 16 hr, cells in the ventricular part of the network showed longer calcium transient rise time (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b) but faster inter-cellular spread of activation (Figure 2g–l, Figure 2—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: Observation from the authors' longitudinal analysis shown in figures.

claim: With organ maturation during 16 hr (36-52 hpf), cells in the ventricular part of the network showed faster inter-cellular spread of activation.
source: With organ maturation during these 16 hr, cells in the ventricular part of the network showed longer calcium transient rise time (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b) but faster inter-cellular spread of activation (Figure 2g–l, Figure 2—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: Observation from the authors' longitudinal analysis shown in figures.

claim: Conduction changed within chambers, such as along the outer curvature in the atrium, during development.
source: Conduction also changed within chambers, such as along the outer curvature in the atrium.
evidence: Observation of regional changes during development from the authors' analysis.

claim: Increasing deformation and twisting of the cardiac tissue was associated with changes in cell shape and in conduction.
source: Increasing deformation and twisting of the cardiac tissue was associated with changes in cell shape (cf. Figure 2d–f) and in conduction (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Correlation observed in the authors' data shown in figures.

claim: Myocardial cells in the two chambers remodel and specialize into functional tissue of working atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes during development.
source: We show functional maturation in line with structural patterning of the heart muscle during development: starting from similar initial states, functionally distinct characteristics of calcium transients and conduction properties develop with a highly reproducible pattern relative to the cell locations (cf. Figure 1—figure supplement 8). Myocardial cells in the two chambers remodel and specialize into functional tissue of working atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes, while cells in the pacemaker and AVC regions continue to resemble the earlier phenotype from the tubular stage.
evidence: Summary interpretation of developmental observations from the authors' study.

claim: Cells in the pacemaker and AVC regions continue to resemble the earlier phenotype from the tubular stage.
source: We show functional maturation in line with structural patterning of the heart muscle during development: starting from similar initial states, functionally distinct characteristics of calcium transients and conduction properties develop with a highly reproducible pattern relative to the cell locations (cf. Figure 1—figure supplement 8). Myocardial cells in the two chambers remodel and specialize into functional tissue of working atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes, while cells in the pacemaker and AVC regions continue to resemble the earlier phenotype from the tubular stage.
evidence: Summary interpretation of developmental observations from the authors' study.

claim: Functionally distinct characteristics of calcium transients and conduction properties develop with a highly reproducible pattern relative to the cell locations.
source: We show functional maturation in line with structural patterning of the heart muscle during development: starting from similar initial states, functionally distinct characteristics of calcium transients and conduction properties develop with a highly reproducible pattern relative to the cell locations (cf. Figure 1—figure supplement 8).
evidence: Summary of developmental patterns observed in the authors' study.

claim: Genetically expressed voltage reporters with improved dynamic range may provide a direct readout of myocardial electrical activity.
source: First, genetically expressed voltage reporters with improved dynamic range may provide a direct readout of myocardial electrical activity.
evidence: Speculation about future technological advancement.

claim: Cameras with higher speed and sensitivity would enhance the recording frequency of rapid volume scanning, needed to explore aberrant myocardial activation during arrhythmias.
source: Second, cameras with higher speed and sensitivity would enhance the recording frequency of rapid volume scanning, needed to explore aberrant myocardial activation during arrhythmias.
evidence: Speculation about future technological advancement and its applications.

claim: The integration of an algorithm capable of tracking cells in 3D during cardiac contractions would allow investigations in fully functional hearts.
source: Third, the integration of an algorithm capable of tracking cells in 3D during cardiac contractions would allow investigations in fully functional hearts.
evidence: Speculation about future methodological advancement.

claim: The addition of optically gated actuators would enable contact-free stimulation to probe the roles of individual cells or groups of cells in pacemaking, conduction, and arrhythmogenesis.
source: Fourth, the addition of optically gated actuators, such as light-activated ion channels or photo-pharmacological probes, would enable contact-free stimulation to probe the roles of individual cells or groups of cells in pacemaking, conduction, and arrhythmogenesis.
evidence: Speculation about future experimental capabilities.

claim: The method opens the way to systematic, scale-bridging, in vivo studies of organogenesis by facilitating cell-accurate measurements across entire organs.
source: It opens the way to systematic, scale-bridging, in vivo studies of organogenesis by facilitating cell-accurate measurements across entire organs.
evidence: Claim about the broader impact and potential of the developed method.

claim: Zebrafish were kept at 28.5°C according to established protocols.
source: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) were kept at 28.5°C and handled according to established protocols (Nusslein-Volhard and Dahm, 2002) and in accordance with EU directive 2011/63/EU as well as the German Animal Welfare Act.
evidence: Description of animal husbandry methods with citation to protocols.

claim: Imaging was performed in live zebrafish embryos between 36 and 52 hr post-fertilization (hpf) at a temperature of 24°C.
source: Imaging was performed in live zebrafish embryos between 36 and 52 hr post-fertilization (hpf) at a temperature of 24°C.
evidence: Description of experimental conditions.

claim: Heart rate at 24°C is 2 Hz, about 0.5 Hz lower than at the temperature recommended for breeding of 28.5°C.
source: Heart rate at this temperature is 2 Hz, about 0.5 Hz lower than at the temperature recommended for breeding of 28.5°C (Baker et al., 1997; Kopp et al., 2005).
evidence: Measurement of heart rate at experimental temperature with comparison to literature values.

claim: Laser power was kept at or below 2 mW in the field of view to exclude thermal effects on heart rate.
source: Laser power was kept at or below 2 mW in the field of view (measured at the back aperture of the illumination objective) to exclude thermal effects on heart rate (an increase in heart rate was detected at laser powers of 5 mW and above).
evidence: Description of experimental parameter control based on observed effects.

claim: An increase in heart rate was detected at laser powers of 5 mW and above.
source: Laser power was kept at or below 2 mW in the field of view (measured at the back aperture of the illumination objective) to exclude thermal effects on heart rate (an increase in heart rate was detected at laser powers of 5 mW and above).
evidence: Experimental observation of laser power effects on heart rate.

claim: The recorded z-stacks of movies were synchronized in time starting at the middle plane and iterating towards first and last plane.
source: The recorded z-stacks of movies were synchronized in time starting at the middle plane and iterating in two independent threads towards first and last plane, respectively.
evidence: Description of data processing method.

claim: Pearson's correlation coefficients were calculated for every cycle in adjacent planes to select the best fit for synchronization.
source: A full cardiac cycle was selected randomly in the middle plane, and Pearson's correlation coefficients were calculated for every cycle in the adjacent plane. The cycle with the highest correlation was selected as the best fit.
evidence: Description of computational method for synchronization.

claim: The presence of both atrial and ventricular myocardium in the majority of planes minimized the risk of false synchronization.
source: As demonstrated before, the presence of both atrial and ventricular myocardium in the majority of planes minimized the risk of false synchronization (Mickoleit et al., 2014).
evidence: Methodological consideration supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Volumes of cell nuclei were extracted from the H2A channel using grayscale blob detection.
source: Volumes of cell nuclei were extracted from the H2A channel of the raw image volumes using grayscale blob detection (Lindeberg, 1998).
evidence: Description of image analysis method with citation to algorithm.

claim: Cell positions were manually curated to resolve potential errors in automated processing.
source: To resolve potential errors in automated processing (false detection, missing cells), cell positions were manually curated using an in-house software (Scherf, 2017) facilitating evaluation, addition and deletion of nuclear positions in the 3D data sets.
evidence: Description of quality control step in data analysis.

claim: The myocardial topology (local connectivity of cells) was estimated by projecting the 3D centroid positions of each cell and its nearest neighbors locally into the 2D Euclidean plane using Singular Value Decomposition.
source: The myocardial topology (local connectivity of cells) was estimated by projecting the 3D centroid positions of each cell and its nearest neighbors locally into the 2D Euclidean plane using Singular Value Decomposition (Bronshtein, 2007) of the 3D centroid positions.
evidence: Description of computational method with citation to mathematical reference.

claim: In each local 2D projection, the cellular connectivity was estimated by computing the 2D Delaunay triangulation.
source: In each local 2D projection, the cellular connectivity was estimated by computing the 2D Delaunay triangulation (Delaunay, 1934).
evidence: Description of computational method with citation to algorithm.

claim: Pacemaker cells were defined as the cells that showed earliest activation and that conducted slowly.
source: Pacemaker cells were defined as the cells that showed earliest activation (activation time shorter than the 0.05-quantile of overall distribution of activation times) and that conducted slowly (conduction speed slower than the median conduction speed within the cell population).
evidence: Description of operational definition used in the analysis.

claim: The approach offers an integrative perspective on tissue and cell levels simultaneously by noninvasively reconstructing the maturation process of the myocardium in its entirety at cellular resolution.
source: By noninvasively reconstructing the maturation process of the myocardium in its entirety at cellular resolution, our approach offers an integrative perspective on tissue and cell levels simultaneously.
evidence: Summary claim about the capabilities of the developed method.

claim: The method demonstrates that myocardial activity can be recorded and analyzed with cellular detail across the entire embryonic heart.
source: We demonstrate that myocardial activity can be recorded and analyzed with cellular detail across the entire embryonic heart.
evidence: Summary of the main technical achievement demonstrated in the study.

claim: The work highlights the value of the zebrafish as a vertebrate model system for in vivo cardiology, especially when combined with high-speed light sheet microscopy and suitable data analysis pipelines.
source: Our work further highlights the value of the zebrafish as a vertebrate model system for in vivo cardiology, especially when combined with high-speed light sheet microscopy and suitable data analysis pipelines.
evidence: Evaluative claim about the significance of the model system and approach.

claim: Organogenesis depends on orchestrated interactions between individual cells and morphogenetically relevant cues at the tissue level.
source: Organogenesis depends on orchestrated interactions between individual cells and morphogenetically relevant cues at the tissue level.
evidence: General biological principle stated as background knowledge.

claim: Heart function critically relies on well-ordered communication between neighboring cells, which is established and fine-tuned during embryonic development.
source: This is true for the heart, whose function critically relies on well-ordered communication between neighboring cells, which is established and fine-tuned during embryonic development.
evidence: General biological principle about cardiac development stated as background knowledge.

claim: For an integrated understanding of the development of structure and function, we need to move from isolated snap-shot observations to simultaneous and continuous cell-to-organ scale imaging.
source: For an integrated understanding of the development of structure and function, we need to move from isolated snap-shot observations of either microscopic or macroscopic parameters to simultaneous and, ideally continuous, cell-to-organ scale imaging.
evidence: Statement of scientific need motivating the study.

claim: The study introduces cell-accurate three-dimensional Ca2+-mapping of all cells in the entire electro-mechanically uncoupled heart during the looping stage of live embryonic zebrafish.
source: We introduce cell-accurate three-dimensional Ca2+-mapping of all cells in the entire electro-mechanically uncoupled heart during the looping stage of live embryonic zebrafish, using high-speed light sheet microscopy and tailored image processing and analysis.
evidence: Summary of the main technical contribution of the study.

claim: The study shows how myocardial region-specific heterogeneity in cell function emerges during early development.
source: We show how myocardial region-specific heterogeneity in cell function emerges during early development and how structural patterning goes hand-in-hand with functional maturation of the entire heart.
evidence: Summary of a main biological finding of the study.

claim: Structural patterning goes hand-in-hand with functional maturation of the entire heart.
source: We show how myocardial region-specific heterogeneity in cell function emerges during early development and how structural patterning goes hand-in-hand with functional maturation of the entire heart.
evidence: Summary of a main biological finding showing correlation between structure and function.

claim: During cardiogenesis, region-specific heterogeneity in cellular activity patterns evolves as the heart undergoes large-scale morphological changes.
source: During cardiogenesis, region-specific heterogeneity in cellular activity patterns evolves as the heart undergoes large-scale morphological changes: The spontaneously active heart tube develops into the mature heart, in which pacemaker cells near the inflow site initiate the rhythmic excitation that spreads with differential velocities through distinct regions of the myocardium.
evidence: General description of cardiac development as background knowledge.

claim: The spontaneously active heart tube develops into the mature heart, in which pacemaker cells near the inflow site initiate the rhythmic excitation.
source: During cardiogenesis, region-specific heterogeneity in cellular activity patterns evolves as the heart undergoes large-scale morphological changes: The spontaneously active heart tube develops into the mature heart, in which pacemaker cells near the inflow site initiate the rhythmic excitation that spreads with differential velocities through distinct regions of the myocardium.
evidence: General description of cardiac development as background knowledge.

claim: In the mature heart, rhythmic excitation spreads with differential velocities through distinct regions of the myocardium.
source: During cardiogenesis, region-specific heterogeneity in cellular activity patterns evolves as the heart undergoes large-scale morphological changes: The spontaneously active heart tube develops into the mature heart, in which pacemaker cells near the inflow site initiate the rhythmic excitation that spreads with differential velocities through distinct regions of the myocardium.
evidence: General description of cardiac physiology as background knowledge.

claim: Controlled cardiac activation gives rise to an orderly sequence of atrial and ventricular calcium release and contraction.
source: This controlled cardiac activation gives rise to an orderly sequence of atrial and ventricular calcium release and contraction.
evidence: General description of cardiac physiology as background knowledge.

claim: An integrated understanding of cardiogenesis at the systems level requires simultaneous cell and organ scale imaging, under physiological conditions in vivo.
source: An integrated understanding of cardiogenesis at the systems level requires simultaneous cell and organ scale imaging, under physiological conditions in vivo.
evidence: Statement of scientific need motivating the study.

claim: The study presents a high-speed light sheet microscopy and data analysis pipeline to measure fluorescent reporters of cardiomyocyte location and activity across the entire electro-mechanically uncoupled heart in living zebrafish embryos during the looping period from 36 to 52 hpf.
source: Here, we present a high-speed light sheet microscopy and data analysis pipeline to measure fluorescent reporters of cardiomyocyte location and activity across the entire electro-mechanically uncoupled heart in living zebrafish embryos during the crucial looping period from 36 to 52 hr post fertilization (hpf).
evidence: Summary of the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The approach has previously required separate experimental setups and specimens to study tissue and cell levels.
source: By noninvasively reconstructing the maturation process of the myocardium in its entirety at cellular resolution, our approach offers an integrative perspective on tissue and cell levels simultaneously, which has previously required separate experimental setups and specimens.
evidence: Statement about limitations of previous approaches, implied by contrast with the new method.

claim: The method opens a new way towards systematic assessment of the mutual interrelations between cell- and tissue properties during organogenesis.
source: Our method opens a new way towards systematic assessment of the mutual interrelations between cell- and tissue properties during organogenesis.
evidence: Claim about the potential impact and applications of the developed method.
